new_packages.label: אוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים וְשִׁין
new_packages.label_en: The Light of the Seven Days and the Letter Shin
new_packages.reason: This package groups three or more concepts that share the same essential nature — primordial supernal light expressed through the structure of the letter shin — forming an independent domain. The Zohar-Arizal concept of the two forms of shin (three-headed and four-headed) representing the light of the seven primordial days is a well-established kabbalistic domain that stands on its own. The four mochin clothed in Binah's vessels being bechina-equivalent to this light creates a coherent cluster: (1) כְּאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים, (2) שִׁין שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁין, (3) שִׁין שֶׁל אַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁין, (4) מֹחִין clothed in נֶצַח-הוֹד-יְסוֹד דְּבִינָה. These four form a self-contained bechina cluster with 4+ nodes and distinct bechina language. This is a new domain not typically covered by standard Wisdom, Prayer, or Malkhut packages in the dataset.

new_packages.mirror_analysis: No explicit evil mirror is visible in this Torah. The text is a positive, constructive fragment focused entirely on the supernal structure of how Malkhut is built and blessed. The absence of an evil counterpart is consistent with the teaching's fragmentary nature — the text ends abruptly with 'עַד כָּאן לְשׁוֹנוֹ זַ"ל' (thus far his language), suggesting it is an incomplete teaching that may have had additional parts not preserved here.

new_packages.label: מַלְכוּת בְּקַטְנוּת
new_packages.reason: A two-node package (Malkhut ↔ 'אוֹשִׁיט פְּסִיעָה לְבַר') is below the threshold of 3+ concepts required for a fully independent new package. However, it is proposed here as a named package because: (a) it is the thematic anchor of the entire teaching — the Torah's opening and problem-statement; (b) it has explicit bechina language; (c) it represents a distinct kabbalistic concept — Malkhut in katnut (smallness) — that differs from the more common Malkhut packages in the dataset which describe Malkhut in its grown/blessed state. The Zohar phrase 'אוֹשִׁיט פְּסִיעָה לְבַר' is itself a technical term for this specific state. Given that this is the subject the Torah seeks to address (to fix and grow Malkhut), it deserves package recognition even at two nodes.

observations: Torah #85 presents an unusual situation: it is the shortest Torah in the LM1 corpus analyzed so far — only 6 lines of text that read as a gloss or fragment attributed explicitly to the Rebbe's own language ('לְשׁוֹן רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה'). The text ends with the marker 'עַד כָּאן לְשׁוֹנוֹ זַ"ל' (thus far his language), indicating it is incomplete or a quoted excerpt from a longer teaching. The dataset has zero edges for reference===85, meaning Torah #85 has not yet been processed into the dataset. The source text contains two distinct bechina domains: (1) A high-kabbalistic cluster equating the four mochin clothed in Binah's vessels with the primordial light of the seven days and the two forms of the letter shin — this is a novel package domain meeting the 3+ node threshold for a new package; (2) A two-node Malkhut-in-katnut cluster describing Malkhut's initial diminished state using the Zohar phrase 'אוֹשִׁיט פְּסִיעָה לְבַר'. The teaching's argument is: Malkhut begins in a diminished state close to Ze'ir Anpin → we want to fix and grow it → this requires illuminating the netzach-hod-yesod of Ze'ir Anpin → which itself requires that Ze'ir Anpin receive mochin → the mochin clothed in Binah's vessels = the light of the seven days = the two forms of shin. The teaching is entirely positive (no evil packages), which is consistent with its role as a kabbalistic how-to instruction for elevating Malkhut.
